title: Private Deployments: VPC & On‑Prem Deployment Guide, Reference Architecture, Day‑2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document provides a consolidated, operationally-focused guide for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on‑prem). It covers reference architectures, on‑prem packaging options, step‑by‑step deployment procedures, day‑2 operations, and the supported upgrade & rollback procedures. Intended audience: SREs, Platform Engineers, Solutions Engineers, and Customer Ops.

Scope

- VPC Private deployment (customer VPC, public/private subnets, customer KMS)
- On‑prem package installation (air‑gapped and online variants)
- Day‑2 operational procedures (monitoring, scaling, backups, troubleshooting)
- Upgrade and rollback playbook (canary, progressive rollout, emergency rollback)
- Customer requirements library (networking, security, capacity sizing)

Reference Architecture (high level)

Components:
- Control Plane: Redwood-managed control plane (optional for fully private installs) or customer-hosted control plane (redwood-control-operator).
- Data Plane: Customer-managed nodes running Redwood runtime (redwood-runtime) in customer VPC or on‑prem cluster.
- Operator / Orchestrator: rp-operator (K8s operator) or rp-deployer (non-K8s install helper).
- Storage: S3-compatible object store for model artifacts, and etcd for operator state.
- Key Management: Customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault, or HSM via PKCS#11).
- Networking: Private subnets for data-plane, public NAT for image pulls (optional for air‑gapped installs), VPC endpoints for object store.

SLOs and Operational Targets:
- Availability target for production clusters: 99.9% monthly for control plane connectivity and API endpoints.
- Performance target: p95 generation latency < 150ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens) on recommended hardware profiles.
- Recovery RTO for node failure: < 5 mins for individual node replacement, < 30 mins for cluster recovery with auto-scaling enabled.

Pre‑deployment checklist (Customer Requirements)

Networking:
- Minimum: 3 private subnets across 3 AZs (cloud) or equivalent racks for on‑prem.
- Required ports (egress/ingress):
  - 443 (HTTPS) outbound to Redwood image registry and control plane (if control plane is external)
  - 2379/2380 (etcd) internal cluster-only
  - 10250, 30000-32767 (K8s node ports, if using K8s)
  - 22 (SSH) restricted to admin CIDRs
- VPC endpoints for S3-compatible storage recommended for model pulls to avoid NAT costs.

Identity & Access:
- Service account with least privilege for object store and KMS operations.
- RBAC: Prepare K8s cluster role bindings for rp-operator with namespace scope.

Capacity sizing (example for typical production workload):
- Small (dev / PoC): 2 x g5.4xlarge or equivalent (8 GPUs total across 2 nodes)
- Medium (low to medium traffic): 4 x g5.12xlarge (48 GPUs total)
- Large (high throughput): 8+ x A100-80GB nodes or equivalent dense GPU fleet

On‑Prem Packaging Options

Supported packaging formats:
- Kubernetes (Helm chart + rp-operator) — recommended for most customers
- Containerized systemd packages (rpm/deb wrappers) for air‑gapped on‑prem without K8s
- VM images (OpenStack/VMware) for customers that prefer VMs

Packaging artifacts:
- Helm repo: registry.redwood.ai/helm/redwood-onprem (chart versioned by release tag)
- Container images: registry.redwood.ai/redwood-runtime:<release>
- Installer binary: rp-deployer-<release>-linux-amd64.tar.gz

Example Helm installation (online):
---
# Add repo and install
helm repo add redwood https://registry.redwood.ai/helm
helm repo update
helm upgrade --install redwood-release redwood/redwood-onprem --namespace redwood --create-namespace --values ./platform-values.yaml
---

Air‑gapped install notes:
1) Mirror required images to customer registry using mirror-list provided in release bundle.
2) Provide offline package containing helm charts, rp-deployer binary, and signatures.
3) Ensure KMS/HSM connectivity (or configure local software KMS for air‑gapped evaluation).

Deployment steps — VPC (Kubernetes)

1. Prepare cluster and nodes: ensure node labels for gpu, zone, and storage class.
2. Install rp-operator (rbac, crds): kubectl apply -f rp-operator-crds.yaml
3. Create namespace and secrets:
   - object-store credentials (redwood-objectstore-creds)
   - kms credentials (redwood-kms-creds)
4. Deploy runtime (CR): create RedwoodRuntime CR with model catalog pointers, nodeSelector for GPUs, and autoscaling policy.
5. Verify preflight: rpctl preflight --namespace redwood --check networking, storage, kms
6. Canary rollout: start with 1 replica of runtime in a canary namespace, run smoke tests (latency, model quality) for 24 hours.
7. Gradual scale to production traffic using routing policies in control-plane or local ingress.

Command examples:
- rpctl status --namespace redwood
- kubectl get pods -n redwood -o wide
- rpctl logs redwood-runtime-0 --follow

Day‑2 Operations

Monitoring & Alerts:
- Integrations provided: Prometheus metrics endpoint, Grafana dashboards, and OpenTelemetry traces.
- Key alerts (examples):
  - Node GPU memory pressure > 90% (SEV: P1)
  - Model load failure rate > 1% in 5m (SEV: P1)
  - Control-plane heartbeat missing > 2m (SEV: P1)
  - Image pull failures > 5% for > 10m (SEV: P2)

Common operational tasks:
- Scaling up: Update node pool (cloud) or provision additional rack capacity (on‑prem), then update runtime CR to increase replicas.
- Model rollout: Publish new model version to object store, update runtime CR with version pin and rollout policy (canary %).
- Rotating KMS keys: Follow KMS provider rotation process and update redwood-kms-creds secret; trigger rolling restart of runtime pods.

Backups & Disaster Recovery:
- Back up etcd snapshots daily and before upgrades.
- Store model artifacts in immutable object storage with lifecycle rules for retention.
- Recovery test quarterly: restore etcd snapshot to dev environment and validate model serving.

Upgrade & Rollback Procedures

Principles:
- Upgrades are staged: canary -> small cohort -> full rollout.
- Keep database/state migrations backwards-compatible where possible.
- Always capture etcd snapshot and configuration bundle prior to any upgrade.

Canary Upgrade Procedure (K8s/operator-based):
1. Snapshot etcd: etcdctl snapshot save /backups/etcd-$(date +%F).db
2. Tag release and prepare image/helm values.
3. Deploy to canary namespace: helm upgrade --install redwood-canary redwood/redwood-onprem --namespace redwood-canary --values canary-values.yaml
4. Run smoke tests (end-to-end synthetic traffic, model quality tests, latency benchmarks) for >= 4 hours.
5. If green, advance to 10% traffic cohort using routing rules; monitor for regressions for 24 hours.
6. Gradually increase to 50% and then 100% with health checks and automated rollback triggers.

Automated rollback triggers:
- Error rate increase > 2x baseline for 10m
- p95 latency increase > 50% for 10m
- Severe memory or OOM events across > 2 nodes

Emergency rollback steps:
1. Pause ingress routing to affected release and re-route to previous stable release.
2. helm rollback redwood-release <previous_revision> or reapply previous manifest bundle.
3. If migration caused incompatible state, restore etcd from snapshot and follow data recovery runbook.

Rollback checklist:
- Confirm snapshot integrity and timestamps.
- Communicate to stakeholders (customers, SEs, oncall).
- Open incident if rollback is triggered outside maintenance window.

Troubleshooting Playbook (common issues)

Issue: Model artifacts failing to load
- Check object store permissions: rpctl check-objectstore
- Verify model checksum and artifact path in runtime CR
- Confirm network egress to object store or mirror registry

Issue: High token latency under load
- Inspect batching settings in runtime CR and rp-operator logs
- Scale out worker replicas or increase batch size (tradeoff: cost vs latency)
- Enable prefix caching if workload exhibits repeated prefixes

Customer Requirements Library (quick reference)

Network:
- Minimum three AZ spread (cloud) or three physical racks (on‑prem)
- Dedicated management VPC peering for control plane (if using Redwood-managed control plane)

Security:
- TLS for all control and data plane endpoints (mutual TLS for control-plane <-> data-plane recommended)
- KMS integration required for customer-managed keys for model-at-rest encryption

Compliance:
- Audit logging retained for 90 days by default; longer retention available as add-on

Appendix A — Example runtime CR (trimmed)

apiVersion: redwood.ai/v1
kind: RedwoodRuntime
metadata:
  name: redwood-runtime-prod
  namespace: redwood
spec:
  modelCatalog: s3://models.redwood/customer-x/catalog.json
  nodeSelector:
    accelerator: nvidia-gpu
  autoscaling:
    minReplicas: 2
    maxReplicas: 24
  batching:
    enabled: true
    maxBatchSize: 32
  kms:
    provider: aws-kms
    keyId: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-ef01
